summary: A proposal to start discussion on a network Data Management System, or Data Control Facility, building on tools like NCP and Telnet. It is a framework, not a full design, aimed at letting users share data more easily.

eli5.summary: A first sketch for a service that helps different computers share and manage data. The author asks for comments.

subtitle: A framework for a network data management service enabling sites to share and access data reliably.

tldr.problem: The ARPA network needed a standardized system for sharing data across sites, but a complete design was missing.
tldr.mechanism: D. B. McKay proposes a Data Control Facility (DCF) architecture with six components: user interface via Telnet, a central DCF coordinator, a network catalog, a form machine for data conversion, remote DCF peers, and file transfer protocol integration.
tldr.outcome: The proposal provides a framework for subsequent protocol development and implementation of network data sharing, building on existing network infrastructure.

today: RFC 304 from February 1972 presents early architectural thinking on network data management. Though not a protocol specification, it provided a conceptual framework that influenced subsequent development of network resource sharing and data protocols.

sections.title: The Problem and Approach
sections.content:
D. B. McKay of IBM submitted this proposal to open discussion on designing a network Data Management System. It is explicitly a framework, not a complete design, aimed at helping the community recognize and develop necessary tools in a unified way.

The proposal builds on existing network infrastructure like NCP, Telnet, and the Form Machine. The goal is to bring data-sharing capability to users in a way that is consistent with how other major network services have evolved.
sections.eli5: McKay sketches a service that lets different sites share data by building on tools the network already has.

sections.title: The System Architecture
sections.content:
McKay identifies six functional components. A user interface through Telnet lets users issue commands interactively. A Data Control Facility (DCF) coordinates all activity and interfaces with other components. A network catalog stores metadata about all shareable data.

A form machine handles data conversion when different sites need different formats. Remote DCF peers (DCF') handle requests at each site. Finally, the file transfer protocol provides the actual data movement between sites, with acknowledgments sent back to the coordinating DCF.
sections.eli5: The system has six parts: a command interface for users, a coordinator, a data directory, a converter for different formats, remote helpers, and a way to send files.

sections.title: Data Language and Catalog
sections.content:
The proposal suggests building on the Data Language developed by Computer Corporation of America. Data is organized in nested containers with types like STRING, INT, REAL, ARRAY, LIST, STRUCT, and MIX. Users access data by concatenating qualified names reflecting logical nesting.

The network catalog has two segments: a local directory recording metadata about data stored locally, and a distributed directory tracking replicated data and pointers to remote files. The catalog can be kept at multiple locations for reliability, with periodic updates propagating changes from local segments to the network segment.
sections.eli5: Data is organized like boxes inside boxes, and a directory keeps track of where each piece of data lives and how to get it.

sections.title: Key Operations and Services
sections.content:
The proposal describes essential operations: CREATE, DELETE, OPEN, TRANS, CLOSE, and DEFINE commands manage data. Subscripting allows retrieval of parts of large containers. The form machine can translate data automatically to the format needed by the requesting application.

A crucial feature is implicit file transfer: a DCF at one site can request a file from a DCF at another site and have it sent to a third site without the user managing each connection explicitly. This removes complexity from the user's perspective while maintaining the underlying file transfer protocol.
sections.eli5: Users can create, delete, or ask for pieces of data. The system automatically converts formats and moves files between sites as needed.
